t: You're looking at the monument to Major-General James Wolfe inside Westminster Abbey. Wolfe was a British Army officer, known for his training reforms, and remembered above all for his victory over the French at the Battle of the Plains of Abraham in Quebec in 1759. He was killed in action in the final moments of that battle. The monument was made by Joseph Wilton, an English sculptor who was a founding member of the Royal Academy and made many memorials to famous Britons in the Abbey.
